subject: Estoicismo

learner_context.prior_exposure: informal only (social media summaries and loose quotes); confirmed no reading of primary texts by Sêneca, Epicteto or Marco Aurélio

confirmed_competencies: Intuitive and correct grasp of the 'dicotomia do controle' (separating what depends on oneself -- reactions, choices -- from what does not -- external events)
Able to apply that idea to a plausible everyday scenario (a delayed flight) with a coherent, correct Stoic-style response
Clear, concrete motivation for practical application: wants calmer reactions to traffic and work delays by focusing on their own response instead of the external event
knowledge_gaps: No familiarity with primary texts or authors beyond recognizing names in passing (Sêneca, Epicteto, Marco Aurélio) -- confirmed again in this follow-up session

No confirmed knowledge of the four Stoic cardinal virtues (sabedoria, coragem, justiça, temperança): the follow-up question about them went unanswered across three separate reply attempts on this session, so this remains an open gap rather than a demonstrated competency
No formal vocabulary or framework for Stoic ethics beyond the dichotomy of control (e.g. cardinal virtues, Stoic logic/physics, oikeiosis, virtue as the sole good)
No knowledge of historical context or the development of the Stoic school

recommended_starting_depth.notes: Confirmed in a follow-up session: the learner has no formal exposure to Stoicism but already holds a correct informal intuition about the dichotomy of control and can apply it to a real scenario, plus a clear personal motivation (calmer reactions to traffic/work delays). The path should start from first principles (history, key authors, foundational vocabulary including the four cardinal virtues) rather than re-teaching the dichotomy of control from scratch, while still formalizing and deepening that concept early on.

material_caveats: This was a bounded 4-question follow-up/confirmation session for a subject with a prior diagnostic already on record; it refines rather than replaces that placement.

The question about the four cardinal virtues was left unanswered in all three reply attempts recorded on this session issue (the learner's replies answered questions 1, 2 and 4 each time, renumbering them inconsistently, but never answered the virtues question) -- evidence_sufficiency is recorded as limited for that reason, and the existing conservative assumption (no knowledge of the cardinal virtues) was kept rather than assumed resolved.
Broader curriculum gaps (e.g. Stoic physics/logic, other philosophers) are expected to be covered as regular curriculum topics rather than further diagnostic probing.
